headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and call APIs, creating default-path leakage and downstream error risks when paired with a non-runnable knowledge list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between awesome-selfhosted and PaddleOCR, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external file handoff into PaddleOCR’s document pipeline, which is an unusual configuration. Because uncertainty must escalate, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF an operator copies awesome-selfhosted content into PaddleOCR as document text or browser input, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted content.
Require manual review before OCR-ing any list content.
Use a provenance note in filenames or tickets.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and shows no data classes touched, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images and can call APIs with allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or secrets, so leakage is limited to document contents if an operator routes them through PaddleOCR. The pairwise pathway exists but the blast radius is small to moderate.
conditions: IF documents from the knowledge-management workflow are sent to PaddleOCR, those contents may leave the local boundary via allowlisted API calls.
IF the two agents are placed in a shared workspace, accidental exposure becomes more likely.
mitigations: Do not send sensitive documents to PaddleOCR.
Use a separate scratch directory for OCR inputs.
Review outbound API destinations before processing.
Strip secrets from documents before OCR.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no write surfaces, while PaddleOCR exposes API calls and browser execution but no filesystem or git write capability is documented. Without overlapping mutable resources, a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk would emerge.
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate directories.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Do not grant filesystem write access unless needed.
Use serialized job scheduling if writes are added.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can transform documents/images into downstream outputs, so if awesome-selfhosted content is fed into it, the second agent may render or act on OCR results without verification. The pair lacks any documented validation or provenance controls, so an error in the first agent can cascade into the second agent’s outputs in default use.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is treated as authoritative downstream, OCR mistakes or misread list entries propagate.
IF the workflow uses OCR results without a human verification step, cascading errors become likely.
mitigations: Add a human verification step after OCR.
Compare OCR output against the source document.
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review.
Limit downstream automation to verified fields only.
requires-engineering: add provenance and confidence propagation.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention obligations are documented for awesome-selfhosted, and PaddleOCR only shows documents/images plus allowlisted egress. Because the profiles do not specify regulated data classes or mismatched jurisdictions, compliance risk is limited to generic handling gaps rather than a concrete breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated documents are introduced into PaddleOCR, residency or retention controls may need review.
IF the operator relies on undocumented retention behavior, compliance gaps can appear.
mitigations: Avoid regulated documents in the OCR pipeline.
Document retention settings before use.
Confirm outbound API destinations.
Delete temporary OCR artifacts promptly.
requires-engineering: add policy controls for residency and retention.
